title: な versus の, and なる / たる adjectives
summary: Japanese is noun-centered: な-adjectives, の-adjectives and する-verbs are all nouns. な is the copula before a noun, の links a noun to a noun, and なる / たる are old-style forms.

blocks.text: The course models a sentence as a **train**: three kinds of **engines** (verbs, い-adjectives, and noun + だ) pull noun **carriages** marked by particles. Almost everything that is not an engine is a noun, even words dictionaries file under "adjective".
A word like 綺麗 is a **noun** that is used as a description. The copula だ becomes **な** before a noun, so だ and な are the same word.
Some such words also work as ordinary nouns and take particles: 元気 (healthy) can be 元気な子供, but also 元気を出して ("cheer up"). Only nouns take case particles like を, so that proves it.
Any noun can describe another with **の**: 魔法の帽子, a magic hat. Some words take either: 不思議な国 makes the country itself strange, while 不思議の国 keeps 不思議 more noun-like, a country of wonder.
A noun + **する** becomes a verb: 勉強 + する = 勉強する. It is the one big exception where an imported noun really acts as a verb.

Two nouns can simply sit side by side: 本棚 (bookshelf), 日本語 (the Japanese language). In longer chains each noun describes the one after it. A word written only in kanji, with no okurigana, is almost always a noun.
なる and たる: the literary forms
Words like 華麗なる探偵 or 堂々たる態度 sound old-fashioned and grand. They are nouns too, in an old-style attributive form, and work like "magnificent" in a title.

items: **Noun + な + noun**: an adjectival noun described by the copula.
**Noun + の + noun**: any noun modifies another.
**なる / たる**: grand, literary descriptive forms.

questions.instruction: What is the な in 綺麗な花?
options: The copula だ in its before-a-noun form
questions.note: だ and な are the same copula.

questions.instruction: What does の do in 魔法の帽子?
Which word can take both な and の?
questions.note: 不思議な国 and 不思議の国 both exist.

questions.instruction: What is 勉強する made of?
options: The noun 勉強 + する

questions.note: Nouns can sit side by side.

questions.instruction: What feel does 華麗なる探偵 have?

questions.prompt: Words traditionally called な-adjectives are really nouns.
questions.note: Hence 元気を出して works.
Adjectival noun + な before the noun.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun carrying a case particle (proof it is a noun)

questions.note: 魔法 is an ordinary noun, so it takes の.
綺麗 takes な, not の.
